pr_body: This PR fixes https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/595 when the user responds with a value where no compatible serializer exists. The result is a hanging request with no errors. It's better to fail first instead to convert the payload somehow.
pr_comments:
This doesn't actually solve issue #595. All it does is produce a different error message.

The real problem is that the error is getting caught [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/44e76f84675181afe3c68d52f71f5a3a4f7f86f0/lib/handleRequest.js#L120-L122) and then a response is not sent because `reply.sent` is `true` [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/44e76f84675181afe3c68d52f71f5a3a4f7f86f0/lib/reply.js#L32) so the request hangs forever.
Indeed, this would be a great use case for a system error introduced in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/591. We could throw errors From type `TypeError` instead `Error` and let it crash.

@mcollina @delvedor Do you think this is really necessary? `res.end()` already does this check and throws a `TypeError` with the message "First argument must be a string or buffer". This seems like added complexity and more code running in a hot path just to get a slightly better error message.

@nwoltman I tend to agree with you, but the check is at the end of the `if else if` chain, I don't think that the impact is sensible.
Indeed I can agree with you for the check after the custom serializer.

@nwoltman that's right an error is already thrown but the message is consistent with the others and it contains the context which value you have passed that's the difference of a developer-friendly framework IMO :)

Alright I'll amend my previous statement and say that it's a _much_ better error message. It's a trade-off though: better developer experience vs. performance. Sometimes you have to choose between them and it's hard to know which one to choose.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: Response with Content-Type set and object payload hangs in fastify ^0.35.7
comments:
Hi @rabbitmeow it depends on the content-type. You can't pass json and send it as `text/html`. You have to do:

```js
fastify
  .get('/', schema, async function (req, reply) {
    reply.type('text/html')
    reply.send(JSON.stringify(req.headers))
  })
```
I know that. But the previous version would throw an error.
Please always write this on the issue. I could reproduce it.

review_comments: That's what I thought initially too, but the `payload` changes on the line above so it's a different value.
